rubric.why: The table is enclosed in the table element.

rubric.why: Rows and cells form the contents of an HTML table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming or showing <tr> with <td> or <th>.

modelAnswer:
Use the and
tags to mark the beginning and end of a table.

items.followUp: What is the output of an AND operation when one input is false?

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing AND as a Boolean or logical operator.

rubric.why: The AND result is true only if all its inputs are true.
rubric.description: States the condition for a true result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that all inputs must be true for the output to be true.

modelAnswer: It gives a true output only when all its inputs are true; otherwise, the output is false.

items.followUp: In which year was Boolean Algebra developed, and who developed it?

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying George Boole.

rubric.description: Gives the year of its invention.

modelAnswer: Boolean Algebra was invented by George Boole in 1854.

items.followUp: What happens to the data stored in volatile memory when the power is switched off?

rubric.why: Volatile memory temporarily holds data and instructions in use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it temporarily stores data or instructions.

rubric.why: Volatile memory requires power to retain its contents.
rubric.description: Explains what happens when power is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its contents are lost when the power is switched off.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory temporarily stores the data and instructions currently being used by the computer.
It needs power to retain its contents, so the stored data is lost when the power is switched off.

items.followUp: Give two examples of communication channels used to transmit data.

rubric.why: A communication channel is the medium or path through which data travels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a medium or path for transmitting data.

rubric.why: The channel carries data from a sender to a receiver.
rubric.description: States the role of the channel in communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that it carries data between communicating devices or parties.

modelAnswer: A communication channel is the medium or path through which data is transmitted from a sender to a receiver.

items.followUp: Which protocol is commonly used to send e-mail messages?

rubric.why: SMTP is the standard protocol used to send e-mail.

modelAnswer: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send e-mail messages.

items.followUp: What does a server do after receiving a request from a client?

rubric.why: Communication begins when the client sends a request to the server.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the client sends a request to the server.

rubric.why: The server processes the request and returns a response to the client.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the server responds to the client.

modelAnswer: The client sends a request to the server over a network.
The server processes the request and sends a response back to the client.

items.followUp: How can a user access a file stored in Google Drive from another device?

rubric.why: Google Drive stores files online using cloud storage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Google Drive as an online or cloud storage service.

rubric.why: Users can access and share stored files through the internet.
rubric.description: States a practical use of the service.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning access to or sharing of files over the internet.

modelAnswer: Google Drive is a cloud storage service that lets users store files online.
Users can access and share their files over the internet from different devices.
